name: Manasseh
bio:
Manasseh is the firstborn son of Joseph and his Egyptian wife Asenath. Joseph named him saying, "God hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house" — reflecting the comfort Joseph finally found after his years of suffering in Egypt (Genesis 41:51). On his deathbed, Jacob specifically adopted Joseph's two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, as his own, giving them equal standing with his other sons to inherit as tribes of Israel (Genesis 48:5).

Yet when Jacob blessed the two grandsons, he laid his right hand on the younger Ephraim's head and his left hand on the firstborn Manasseh's — Joseph tried to correct him, but Jacob insisted, saying that though Manasseh too would become a great people, his younger brother Ephraim would become greater still (Genesis 48:13-20), continuing the recurring Genesis theme of the younger prevailing over the elder.
